slides.title: What counts as one?
points: No prior afebrile seizure, no metabolic cause
slides.highlight: Most common seizure type in childhood

slides.title: Simple vs complex
slides.subtitle: Simple || Complex
points: No post-ictal deficit || May leave Todd's palsy
slides.highlight: Any ONE complex feature = complex febrile seizure

slides.title: Red flags: think beyond
points: **Neck stiffness**, bulging fontanelle → rule out meningitis
slides.highlight: LP if signs of meningitis, or consider if <12 months & unimmunised

slides.title: Recurrence risk: YOUNG
points: Y - Young age at onset (<18 months)
O - Only brief fever before seizure
U - Under 40°C at time of seizure
G - Grows with each factor present

slides.title: Exam pearls
points: Simple FS: **no routine EEG or neuroimaging**
Epilepsy risk only slightly above general population
slides.highlight: Reassure parents: simple FS has an excellent prognosis
